notes: Found by job-scout; Berlin hybrid ~70% on-site; recruiter posting, client unnamed (VC-backed AI healthcare/medical info startup), ask name + salary vs Blue Card; gaps frontend depth/TypeScript, product analytics/user-behaviour data; Mid-Senior
apply_hint: Apply via the LinkedIn posting (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4483366465). JuicyLemons is a recruiter; the client is an unnamed, VC-backed Berlin start-up using AI for medical and clinical information for healthcare professionals and patients.
verdict: Solid on the AI side and on "build the whole thing": full web apps with a React frontend and Python/FastAPI backend (Expert Interface on Azure, Covestro agentic app on AWS), AI/ML-driven products, cloud on AWS and Azure, close work with the people who use the tool (SAP experts, chemists, business stakeholders), and small-team start-up experience reporting to a CTO. Weaker on what makes this a *product* engineer role: frontend depth (React is listed as beginner in the base CV, no TypeScript/Next.js), data-informed prioritisation from user behaviour (no product analytics in the profile), formal testing, and the "Mid-Senior" level. No healthcare work experience.

form_fields.label: Why this company?
form_fields.value: Medical information is a field where an unclear answer has a real cost, and the same fact has to read differently for a doctor and a patient. I want to work on that product problem in a small team, close to the founders and the users.

form_fields.label: Salary expectation
form_fields.value: €70,000 gross/year (range €60,000–75,000). Must be above the EU Blue Card threshold.

form_fields.label: Location
form_fields.value: will be based in Berlin; hybrid ~70% on-site is fine.

questions.q: Tell us about a time you spotted friction for users and changed the product.
questions.a: Expert Interface at Kniit: the knowledge graph was only useful if SAP experts could check it, so you built one place to review, validate and approve changes. Covestro data science internship: chemists could try parameter changes in the Streamlit dashboard before running a physical batch. After building the project: the one UX change the funnel data prompted.

questions.q: How do you decide what to build next / how do you use data?
questions.a: Ground-truth evaluation at Kniit: measure, find the biggest error class, fix it (33/45 → 93/90 precision/recall). Choosing a deterministic pipeline for the high-volume source because the cost data said so ($200k projected LLM budget → near zero). Be honest that you have not run product analytics or A/B tests in a job; the project shows the basics.

questions.q: Walk us through the architecture of a web app you built, frontend to backend, and how you tested it.
questions.a: Covestro: React frontend, FastAPI backend, Postman API tests, Docker, AWS CDK, GitLab CI/CD. Kniit Expert Interface: React + Python microservices on Azure. Be honest about React depth (two internal apps, no TypeScript in a job).
